descriptive_title: Grade 3 Mathematics: Algebra (Coding) — Sequential, Concurrent, and Repeating Events Without Screens (C3.1-C3.2)
subject: Mathematics

curriculum_expectations.C3.1: solve problems and create computational representations of mathematical situations by writing and executing code, including code that involves sequential, concurrent, and repeating events
curriculum_expectations.C3.2: read and alter existing code, including code that involves sequential, concurrent, and repeating events, and describe how changes to the code affect the outcomes

unit_overview: A 5-day Grade 3 unit on coding without screens (C3.1-C3.2) framed around 'Bug Busters' — Buzz the Bug-Buster Beetle and Patch the Repair Pup. Day 1 introduces concurrent events. Day 2 writes code with concurrent events. Day 3 reads code and finds bugs. Day 4 alters buggy code to fix it. Day 5 closes with child-invented bug-busting projects. Each lesson includes an expanded_walkthrough.
unit_learning_goal: Children will write and execute code with sequential, concurrent, and repeating events; read and alter buggy code; and describe how changes affect outcomes.

lesson_arc.big_idea: Some events happen AT THE SAME TIME (concurrent) instead of one after another. Two robots moving at once = concurrent.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can identify and write code with concurrent events.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Buzz introduces concurrent events; children identify which events run at the same time vs in order.

lesson_arc.big_idea: Concurrent code uses parallel lanes. Two actions in the same time-step run together.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can write code with concurrent events.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Children write 2-lane code: one robot does X while the other does Y, all in the same time-step.

lesson_arc.big_idea: A BUG is a problem in code that makes the outcome wrong. Bug Busters find bugs by tracing code carefully.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can find a bug in existing code and explain it.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Children read code with planted bugs; trace and identify what went wrong.

lesson_arc.big_idea: We fix bugs by altering the code. Change the wrong step, the wrong number, or the wrong order.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can fix a bug by altering the code.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Children take buggy code and alter it to produce the correct outcome.

lesson_arc.big_idea: We can write our own code AND plant a bug for a partner to find.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can write code, plant a bug, and check my partner's fix.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Children write code with concurrent events, plant a bug, swap, debug, share.

recurring_characters.name: Buzz the Bug-Buster Beetle
recurring_characters.role: Lead character. A friendly beetle with a magnifying glass and a wrench. Anchors all 5 lessons.
recurring_characters.visual_description: A friendly beetle with a hard hat, magnifying glass, wrench, big eyes. Cheerful smile, antenna with bug detector.

recurring_characters.name: Patch the Repair Pup
recurring_characters.role: Buzz's partner. The 'fix-it' character. Cameo Lessons 2-5.
recurring_characters.visual_description: A young dog with a tool belt and bandage roll. Eager expression, tail wagging.

threaded_vocabulary.child_friendly_definition: Happening one after another in order.
Doing the same thing many times (a loop).
A problem in code that makes the outcome wrong.

manipulatives_index.name: 2-Lane Coding Grid Mat
manipulatives_index.description: Letter-size mat with 2 robot lanes for concurrent code.

manipulatives_index.name: Bug Type Anchor Chart
manipulatives_index.description: Chart of common bug types: wrong step, wrong number, wrong order.

materials_overview: Bug Buster Capstone Templates (1 per child)

assessment_strategy.formative: Lesson 2 writing tracker; Lesson 3 finding tracker; Lesson 4 fixing tracker.

pedagogical_notes: C3.1 with concurrent events is the Grade-3 expansion. Use 2-lane mat to visualise.
Bugs are normal. Frame them as part of coding, not failure.
Trace code carefully — bugs hide in subtle places.
Alteration to fix a bug is the same skill as altering for any reason.
Concurrent events parallel real-world simultaneity — cooking 2 dishes, 2 kids playing.
canadian_context_notes: Concurrent: 2 hockey games at the same time on different rinks.
Sequential: Tim Hortons line — order, then pay, then receive.
Repeating: skating laps around the rink.
